name: Data Steward
summary: Monday: full history from FRED (49 series), EIA (4), Massive (17 ETFs), GPR, NY Fed GSCPI and CAPE. Wednesday: an incremental refresh, 71 requests asking only for data newer than what was stored. Keys read from the environment; raw payloads hashed and stored. Option quotes, Greeks and implied-vol ranks came from Interactive Brokers (read-only market-data tools): 26 quotes Monday pre-market, 10 more at Tuesday's close.

name: Global Liquidity & Dollar
summary: Liquidity is draining at the margin but conditions are still loose. US net liquidity fell $79bn over 13 weeks as the Treasury holds about $1tn of cash and reverse repo is down to $0.4bn, so reserves are doing the draining. Financial conditions stay easy and M2 grows near 6%. The dollar firmed to its 81st percentile of 10 years; the yen's three-month gain shrank to about 1%, easing the carry-unwind worry.
findings: US net liquidity (Fed assets - TGA - reverse repo) is $5,746bn, down $79bn in 13 weeks. | Treasury cash is about $1,000bn and reverse repo only $0.4bn, so reserves fell $91bn in 13 weeks. | Financial conditions are loose (NFCI -0.49) and M2 is up 5.71% year on year. | The broad dollar sits at its 81st percentile of 10 years; USD/JPY is down only 1.06% in 3 months.

name: Rates, Central Banks & Credit
summary: The Fed is in a hiking cycle: it raised rates in September and held at 3.75-4.00% in October with two hawkish dissents, and the 2-year yield sits 71bp above Fed funds, pricing more hikes. Real 10-year yields of 2.62% are restrictive. Long-run inflation expectations remain anchored. High-yield spreads have widened 33bp in a month to 3.43%, an early warning. The hurdle rate is 3.88%.
findings: Effective Fed funds is 3.88%, up 24bp in six months; the October meeting held with hawkish dissent. | The 2-year yield (4.59%) is 71bp above Fed funds, implying further hikes are priced. | The 10-year real yield is 2.62%, up 19bp in three months; 5y5y inflation expectations are anchored at 2.21%. | High-yield spreads widened 33bp in a month to 3.43%; investment-grade spreads are 0.94%.

name: Growth & Inflation Nowcast
summary: Growth is positive but fading and inflation is re-accelerating. Claims are low, GDPNow rose to 3.7% and the Philly Fed is strong, but payroll growth has slowed to 51k a month. Headline CPI is 4.0% as energy feeds through, core CPI is running 3.4% annualized over three months, and one-year inflation expectations are 4.6%. The growth composite slipped from 0.38 to 0.26 while inflation rose from 0.17 to 0.49.
findings: Growth composite 0.26, down from 0.38 three months ago; payrolls 3-month average only 51k; GDPNow 3.74%. | Labor market still tight on claims: 4-week average 197k, down 13.2% year on year; unemployment 4.2%. | Inflation composite rose from 0.17 to 0.49: headline CPI 4.02% y/y, core CPI 3.41% annualized over 3 months. | Consumers expect 4.6% inflation over the next year.

name: Geopolitics & Policy Risk
summary: Geopolitical risk is still very high but easing at the margin. The 30-day Geopolitical Risk average fell to 164 (90th percentile of 10 years), and the daily reading dropped to 98 on November 2, the same day oil fell about 7%; news sources do not yet confirm why. The US-Israel-Iran conflict and Hormuz attacks remain the main channel to oil. Midterm results (Nov 3) are not yet confirmed in our sources; policy uncertainty is at its 81st percentile.
findings: 30-day average GPR is 164, at the 90th percentile of 10 years and down 5 points in three months; the daily reading fell to 98 on November 2. | Attacks near a Saudi oil port and in the Strait of Hormuz pushed Brent back to $110 in mid-October; tanker attacks escalated. | US economic policy uncertainty (30-day) is at its 81st percentile of 10 years.

name: Global Supply Chain
summary: Supply chains are under above-normal pressure. The NY Fed's pressure index is 1.28, at its 87th percentile of 20 years and still rising, consistent with Gulf shipping disruption. Inventories are lean relative to sales. This adds to goods inflation over the next one to two quarters.
findings: GSCPI is 1.28 (September), at its 87th percentile of 20 years, up 0.08 in three months. | Inventories-to-sales ratio 1.33, down 0.07 in a year: little buffer.

name: Crude Oil & Natural Gas
stance_label: Crude tight but cracking; gas loose
summary: Crude is in a war-driven supply shock. WTI is $103 (up 66% in a year) and Brent $123, and the $20 Brent-WTI gap says the shortage is in seaborne barrels, while US supply is ample (Cushing 11% above its 5-year norm, output up 2.7%). US crude stocks fell 16.7mb in four weeks. But USO dropped about 7% on November 2, cutting its one-month gain to 6.4%, as geopolitical-risk readings eased; FRED crude prices lag to October 27. Oil implied vol (OVX 62.7) is about 25 points above realized: premium is very rich, and the gap risk is now visible. Natural gas is the opposite: storage is above normal and prices are weak.
findings: WTI $103.37, up 66.38% in 12 months and at its 96th percentile of 10 years; Brent $123.10. | Brent trades $19.73 over WTI while Cushing stocks are 11.1% above their 5-year average: the shortage is seaborne. | US crude stocks fell 16.7mb in 4 weeks to 410.6mb, 4.1% below the 5-year average. | OVX 62.69 is about 24.9 points above USO 20-day realized vol: a large volatility premium. | USO's one-month gain shrank to 6.4% after a sharp drop on November 2. | Natural gas storage is 2.2% above the 5-year average and Henry Hub is $2.76.

name: Gold & Silver
summary: Gold and silver are in a sharp correction. GLD is 27% below its 52-week high and 12% under its 200-day average; silver is 58% off its high after a speculative peak. The driver is rising real yields and Fed hike expectations, not a loss of safe-haven demand. Gold's implied vol has risen to mid-range for the year, but its premium over realized vol is still thin. Stand aside until real yields stop rising.
findings: GLD is 27.1% below its 52-week high and 12.4% below its 200-day average. | Silver (SLV) fell 16.8% in a month and is 56.8% below its 52-week high; 20-day realized vol 43%. | The pressure comes from rising real yields (10y real 2.62%, +19bp in 3 months) and hike expectations. | Gold implied vol (GVZ 25.5) is only 3.1 points above realized, at its 47th percentile of the year.

name: US Equities
summary: The S&P 500 trend is intact but narrowing. SPY is 3.1% above its 200-day average and 3.5% off its high, but Nasdaq-100 fell 9.1% in a month and small caps lag. Volatility has woken up: VIX 21, its 87th percentile of the year, with the curve close to inverting. And price is the problem: with a CAPE near 41 and real yields at 2.62%, stocks offer almost no excess yield over bonds, so downside is more likely to be sharp than upside.
findings: SPY is 3.1% above its 200-day average and 3.5% below its 52-week high. | QQQ fell 9.1% in a month (10.3% off its high) with 20-day realized vol of 22.6%. | VIX 21.15 (87th percentile of the year) with VIX/VIX3M 0.979: the curve is close to inverting, a stress warning. | CAPE about 41 against a 2.62% real yield leaves a negative excess CAPE yield.

name: International Equities
summary: International stocks are underperforming as oil importers absorb the energy shock. Emerging markets fell 9.7% in a month and sit below their 200-day average; the Euro Stoxx 50 lags the S&P by 6.5 points over three months; China and India are down 16% and 10% over the year. Japan has held up best. EM implied vol (31.6) is 11 points above realized, so premium is rich, but momentum is negative.
findings: EEM fell 9.7% in a month, is 4.4% below its 200-day average and 14.2% off its high. | Euro Stoxx 50 (FEZ) lags SPY by 6.5 points over 3 months; China (FXI) is down 16.4% and India (INDA) 10.2% over 12 months. | Japan (EWJ) is flat over 3 months (-0.1%), the most resilient major market. | EM implied vol (VXEEM 31.6) exceeds EEM realized vol by 11.1 points.

name: Valuation & CAPE
summary: US stocks are priced near the most expensive level in history. The Shiller CAPE is about 41 (October 2026), above every month of the trailing 10- and 20-year windows in our stored history and second only to the 1999-2000 peak of 44.2. The 10- and 20-year averages are 29.4 and 26.2. Against a 2.62% real yield, the excess CAPE yield is about -0.2%, the weakest valuation cushion in our data. Modifier: US short-put size x0.6, max 12 delta. Global CAPE needs a data provider.
findings: Shiller CAPE about 41.07 for October 2026, near the 44.19 peak of December 1999. | Stored history (to September 2023) gives a 10-year average of 29.4, 20-year 26.2 and long-run 17.4. | Excess CAPE yield = 1/41.07 - 2.62% real yield, about -0.2%.

name: Volatility & Options Surface
summary: Option premium is richest in oil and emerging markets and thinnest in gold. USO implied vol exceeds realized by 24.9 points, EEM by 11.1, SPX by 9.8 and gold by 3.1. Equity vol jumped to its 87th percentile of the year and the VIX curve is nearly flat. Oil premium is rich because the gap risk is real, as Monday showed.
findings: Volatility premium (implied minus 20-day realized): USO 24.9, EEM 11.1, SPX 9.8, GLD 3.1. | VIX at its 87th percentile of the year, just below VIX3M (ratio 0.979). | OVX at the 73rd and VXEEM at the 69th percentile of the year; GVZ at the 47th.

name: Regime Strategist
summary: Shifted 5 points from reflation to stagflation, half of Monday's 10: the inflation impulse is still a war-driven oil supply shock (Brent $123, Brent-WTI $19.7) with payroll growth at 51k a month and the Fed tightening into it (2-year 71bp above Fed funds), but USO fell about 7% on Nov 2 and GDPNow rose to 3.7%, so the stagflation case is weaker than on Monday.

name: CIO / Portfolio Constructor
summary: Collateral still does the heavy lifting: about $1M in T-bills earning roughly the 3.88% Fed funds rate. Since Monday, oil fell about 7%, geopolitical-risk readings eased, and market stress rose (VIX 21, high-yield spreads +33bp in a month). Real IBKR prices show that far out-of-the-money index and bond spreads pay too little for their risk, so XSP and TLT stand aside. One trade is ready if you approve the 10% minimum-credit change: the USO 130/120 December put spread, 13 contracts, about $1,618 credit against $11,382 maximum loss. Under the current 20% rule there is no trade this week. EEM waits for tradable quotes at the open.

name: Red Team
summary: Challenged the plan on ceasefire gap risk, crash correlation, EM momentum, estimated pricing and event timing; every challenge answered by the CIO.

name: Options Structurer
summary: Re-priced on IBKR quotes. USO fell, so the spread moved to 130/120: 12.4% of width at 13 delta with tight quotes. Real put skew leaves XSP at 9.2% and TLT at 7.8% of width (Monday quotes). EEM after-hours quotes were too wide to price.

summary: Election blackout has lifted. Under the current 20% minimum credit no ticket qualifies. USO 130/120 passes every check under the proposed 10% rule: credit, delta cap, quote width, size (max loss $11,382, 1.1% of NAV). Re-check at the open before any fill.
